entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Al-Hakim Abu al-Qasim Ishaq al-Samarqandi was a Sunni-Hanafi scholar, qadi (judge), and sage from Transoxania, renowned for his expertise in Sufism and Islamic jurisprudence. Born in the mid-10th century, he studied under prominent Islamic scholars in Balkh and later became a student of al-Maturidi. Al-Hakim's significance lies in his contributions to the development of Hanafi school of thought, which had a profound impact on Islamic jurisprudence in Central Asia and beyond. His legacy can be seen in the numerous Hanafi madrasas and mosques that still exist in the region today. Through his writings and teachings, Al-Hakim helped shape the intellectual and spiritual landscape of the Islamic Golden Age, leaving an enduring mark on the history of Islamic civilization.
